title: Blurring the Boundaries: Monsters in Dmitry Aleksandrovich Prigov’s “New Anthropology”
core_idea: The article examines Prigov’s use of monstrous, hybrid and androgynous figures across poetry and visual art as a mode of 'new anthropology' that challenges value-laden binaries (human/non-human, official/unofficial, normal/monstrous). Using an interdisciplinary, inter-art and comparative cultural critique informed by Russian and European traditions of monstrosity and personal experience of disability, it analyzes artistic techniques (copying, collage, repetition) and contrasts Prigov’s artistic articulation of posthuman concerns with Western theoretical approaches.
tldr: Analyzes how Prigov’s monstrous hybrid imagery in poetry and art functions as an interdisciplinary 'new anthropology' that problematizes rigid binaries and ideological constructs.
